findings.title: Cleanup deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or state
findings.body: The second arm of the deleteMany OR (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) has no `method: SMS` filter and no `scheduled`/`cancelled` filter. It deletes any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1 across all methods (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) and in any state. The intent is to drop SMS reminders that failed twice, so the clause should be scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false`.

findings.title: Unguarded retry update in catch can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The retryCount update inside the catch block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If that database write fails (connection issue, deleted row, constraint error), the exception escapes the for-loop, so every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped for this run and the handler returns a 500 instead of the 'SMS scheduled' response. One failing reminder can thus block all the others.

findings.title: Reminders with empty message or no sendTo never increment retryCount
findings.body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. If the message is empty (for example no reminderBody and template is not REMINDER) or sendTo is missing, neither the success nor the failure branch runs and retryCount stays at 0. Such a reminder is picked up on every cron run forever and is never deleted, which is the unbounded-retry problem this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of retryCount
findings.body: retryCount is incremented using the value read at the start of the run (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) rather than an atomic `{ increment: 1 }` update. If two cron invocations overlap, both can read the same value and write the same increment, undercounting failures and allowing more attempts than the threshold of two.

findings.title: retryCount is filtered on in the cleanup query but not indexed
findings.body: The new cleanup clause filters on retryCount, and it runs on every cron invocation over the whole WorkflowReminder table. Without an index (the existing indexes cover method/scheduled/scheduledDate and cancelled/scheduledDate only), this forces a full table scan on each run.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry and deletion behavior
findings.body: The PR changes retry counting, the failure path, and the deletion criteria, but adds no tests. Nothing verifies that a reminder is deleted after two failures, that successful scheduling does not increment the counter, or that non-SMS reminders are untouched.
